paper.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1-9 and Appendices A (preliminaries, skimmed), B (algorithm), C (SAE training, reconstruction, decoder geometry, seed stability), D (selection diagnostics, image counterfactuals, from-scratch SAE, random features), E (steering decomposition, feature correspondence), G.2 (bottom-ranked heads); F and H (auto-interpretation and OCR examples) skimmed

claims.claim: The internal features a language model repurposes when it is turned into a vision-language model can be found by warm-starting a sparse autoencoder from the language model's own and adapting it on the multimodal model's text-token activations, then keeping features whose decoder direction rotated most and that respond to images; among these, features that fire more often on a target skill and keep firing under neutral prompts are causally specific to that skill. Supported only if, for spatial-relation questions on three vision-language model families, ablating each of the top such features lowers accuracy on spatial yes/no questions by at least 6 points (mean at least 10) while changing general visual question answering and non-spatial relation questions by at most 3 points; if, on one model, dropping the rotation-and-image filter makes the ablations damage general question answering by more than 20 points, while random features from the same layers move spatial accuracy by less than 1 point; and if an autoencoder trained from scratch on the multimodal activations, selected the same way, yields no feature whose ablation moves spatial accuracy by more than 2 points.
claims.decision_rule: Top spatial features: each dVSR <= -6, mean <= -10 on all 3 models, |dVQA|, |dCtrl| <= 3; no-adapted-filter rules dVQA < -20; random |dVSR| < 1; from-scratch SAE max |dVSR| <= 2.

claims.claim: The same feature-discovery procedure, changing only the set of target prompts, isolates single features that a vision-language model needs for recognising image-dependent unsafe requests and for reading text in images, and removing one such feature suppresses that behaviour without harming other abilities. Supported only if, on PaliGemma 2, ablating the top feature for each of six safety categories of a benchmark where harmful intent is visible only in the image lowers the attack success rate by at least 15 points in every category, and ablating each top text-reading feature lowers accuracy on its OCRBench category by at least 10 points, in both cases with general visual question answering and a matched benign control changing by at most 2 points.
claims.decision_rule: Per-category top safety feature dASR <= -15 on all 6 VLSBench categories; top OCR features dCat <= -10; |dVQA| and |dCtrl| <= 2.

claims.claim: Adding a discovered feature's decoder direction at its own layer, on top of mean-difference activation steering applied at the layers where discovered features live, improves a vision-language model's spatial and text-reading accuracy more than standard single-layer steering. Supported only if, over the top ten spatial and five text-reading features on PaliGemma 2, the mean gain exceeds that of single-layer steering by at least 3 points on spatial relations and 1.5 points on text reading; if injecting the feature direction adds at least 1 point beyond multi-layer steering alone; and if the feature direction on its own gives less than half the gain of single-layer steering.
claims.decision_rule: MMDiff-CAA - CAA >= +3 (VSR) and >= +1.5 (OCR); MMDiff-CAA - multi-layer CAA >= +1; single feature direction < 0.5x single-layer CAA.

experiments.text: Build the dictionaries and the selection pipeline. Setup: LLaVA-MORE (LLaMA-3.1-8B, LLaMA-Scope TopK SAEs, 32K features), PaliGemma 2 (Gemma-2-2B, Gemma-Scope JumpReLU SAEs, 16K) and InternVL3.5-2B (Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen-Scope TopK); one SAE per residual-stream layer warm-started from the base-LM SAE and adapted on 50k VQAv2 image-question pairs with loss on text tokens only. Adapted features: mean squared activation on visual inputs above 0.01 and decoder cosine to the base-LM feature in the bottom 25% (about 5%, 20% and 13% of features). Task features: per-token firing frequency on a target split (spatial VQAv2 questions, VLSBench unsafe prompts, OCR prompts) against generic VQAv2, odds ratio >= 3 and frequency gap >= 0.05 with Fisher tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, kept only if they still fire when the question is replaced by neutral prompts, and intersected with the adapted set (e.g. about 1,400 spatial features for PaliGemma 2, 711 for LLaVA-MORE). Ablation projects the feature's decoder direction out of attention, MLP and residual outputs at every layer, on text tokens only.

Check the dictionary basis before diffing. Setup: compare full-sequence, image-only and text-only adaptation regimes and a randomly initialised SAE on LLaVA-MORE (fraction of variance unexplained, decoder cosine to the base dictionary); on PaliGemma 2, match every feature of the adapted dictionary against the whole base dictionary, and retrain eight layers with a different seed. Result: mean FVU 0.005 for text-only against 0.032 full, 0.037 image-only and 0.050 random, and text-only stays aligned with the base dictionary while the others rotate in early layers. Of 425,974 features, 96.41% are preserved, 3.36% rotate in place, 0% relocate and 0.23% emerge; across seeds the mean same-index cosine is 0.93 and 0.44% of features relocate, 0.98 for the reported top features.

Ablate the top spatial features on three model families. Setup: score each feature on a yes/no VSR subset built from its top-activating samples; report the change in VSR accuracy, in VQAv2 accuracy, and on VSR samples with non-spatial relations (has, wears, holds, made of) as a control. Result: across the top ten features, VSR drops 6.4-15.5 points (mean -10.1) on LLaVA-MORE, 6.9-30.6 (mean -12.3) on PaliGemma 2 and 12.3-17.1 (top eight, mean -14.6) on InternVL3.5; |dVQA| <= 1.5 and control changes between -2.7 and +1.9 points.

Vary the selection rule over the same dictionary. Setup: PaliGemma 2, spatial features, full ablation protocol; random features (one per layer from the same eight layers), contrastive firing only, firing plus image response, firing plus lexical filter, firing plus the rotation-and-image (adapted) filter, and the full pipeline. Result: dVSR / dVQA -0.5 / -0.2 random, -15.1 / -25.9 firing only, -15.9 / -26.3 with image response, -14.6 / -24.4 with the lexical filter, -1.0 / -0.2 with the adapted filter but no lexical filter, and -12.3 / -0.1 for the full pipeline. Rotation without image response selects no features.

Replace diffing with a standard SAE. Setup: an SAE trained from random initialisation on LLaVA-MORE activations with identical data and hyperparameters, top ten spatial features selected by contrastive firing (no base dictionary to diff against). Result: the top features all lie in layer 5 and fire on 100% of VSR samples, saturating the odds ratio; their ablation moves VSR by -1.10 to +1.38 (mean +0.22) against a mean of -10.11 for the diffed features on the same model.

Test whether the spatial features were created by instruction tuning. Setup: ablate the same PaliGemma 2 features in the pretrained checkpoint (pt-448), which has the vision encoder and projector but not multimodal instruction tuning, versus the instruction-tuned one (mix-448). Result: effects are about 3 times larger after instruction tuning (e.g. right side of -2.08 vs -30.62, close to -7.53 vs -18.28); two features have positive effects before and negative after; one (ahead of) is identical in both.

Check that features depend on the image and note how evaluation subsets were chosen. Setup: hold the text fixed and replace the image with another image from the set, a blank grey image or uniform noise, 300 samples per reported feature. Result: mean activation falls by 7.2 / 8.3 / 13.2% for spatial, 4.2 / 21.8 / 8.6% for safety and 16.6 / 36.8 / 28.7% for OCR features, so image dependence is real but modest for spatial and safety features. Each spatial feature is scored on a VSR subset built from its own top-activating samples, and the reported features are the top ten by effect, so per-feature effects overstate the typical candidate (the 1,061-feature safety sweep averages -9.67 against -17 to -28 for the top six).

Ablate safety features. Setup: PaliGemma 2 on VLSBench, where harmful intent is only inferable with the image; attack success judged by Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct; controls are a VQAv2 yes/no subset and the benign MSSBench safe split (baseline ASR about 0), so a rise there would mean spurious unsafe generation. Result: the top feature per category cuts ASR by 28.1 (self-harm), 26.6 (erotic), 26.0 (privacy), 24.4 (violent), 21.1 (hate) and 18.0 points (illegal activity), with dVQA between -0.9 and +0.9 and control changes of 0 to +1.0; across all 1,061 candidates, mean dASR -9.67, dVQA -0.03, dCtrl +0.41. A minority of candidates cause generation collapse rather than refusal and are filtered post hoc.

Ablate text-reading features. Setup: PaliGemma 2, 1,070 OCR-selective features; drop on each feature's OCRBench category (scene text, non-semantic text, digit string, irregular text), VQAv2 and a non-OCR yes/no control. Result: the top five lower their category by 28.0, 16.5, 16.0, 14.0 and 10.0 points (mean -16.9) with |dVQA| <= 1.6 and |dCtrl| <= 1.8.

Compare steering methods. Setup: PaliGemma 2 base; vanilla CAA with one mean-difference direction at a mid layer against MMDiff-CAA (CAA directions added at the discovered features' layers plus the feature's decoder direction scaled 1, 3 or 10 at its own layer); spatial on VSR, OCR reformulated as four-way multiple choice steered at the answer token. Result: spatial mean +12.59 against +8.96 (best feature +30.77 vs +15.38; two of ten features unchanged and two slightly worse); OCR mean +4.02 against +2.21 (one feature +10.58 vs +2.88; one 0.16 lower).

Decompose the steering gain. Setup: same ten spatial features. Result: a single feature direction alone +2.63, all ten feature directions +3.66, single-layer CAA +8.96, multi-layer CAA at the feature layers +10.78, and adding the feature direction +12.59, so layer choice and the injected direction each add about 1.8 points. Attribution patching from each feature back to attention heads (visual tokens replaced by a mean embedding as the corruption) peaks in middle layers near the features' own layers, which motivates the layer choice; bottom-ranked heads do not localise relevant regions (qualitative).

dropped: Auto-interpretation labels (qualitative validation only); threshold sweep (figure only, 'stable'); OCR feature gallery.
notes: Drafted from scratch from arXiv HTML for the dataset50 rebuild, without consulting earlier claims or references. Venue is an ICML 2026 workshop per the arXiv comment; it was in the original 20 and kept as instructed. c0 per-feature bar: smallest top-ten drop 6.38 (LLaVA-MORE); max |dCtrl| 2.71. c2 bars: 12.59-8.96 = 3.63, 4.02-2.21 = 1.81, 12.59-10.78 = 1.81, 2.63/8.96 = 0.29.
